# Documentation review report

_This is the full-depth review format, for docs where the stakes justify it. For
a small or low-stakes doc, a short verdict plus the few issues that matter is
enough — use only the sections below that the doc actually needs, and skip the
rest rather than filling them in._

_File each finding once, in the most severe section that applies. A finding that
blocks belongs under blocking issues, not repeated as a suggestion._

## Summary

_A short overall assessment of the artifact._

## Intended artifact type

_What kind of doc this is meant to be (public user doc, internal note, design
doc, etc.) and the standard it should meet._

## Blocking issues

_Problems that should be fixed before this doc is used or published — or, for a
design, before anyone builds against it._

## Non-blocking suggestions

_Improvements that would help but are not blockers, stated specifically enough to
act on._

## Unsupported or unclear claims

_Statements not backed by evidence, or that are ambiguous._

## Missing reader context

_What a reader needs but the doc does not provide._

## Unsettled user and product questions

_For a design doc: what the design itself has not settled about people — who is
affected, what experience it should enable, whether an "internal" boundary was
decided or assumed, and product decisions sitting inside implementation choices.
These are gaps in the design, not documentation to write later. Technical gaps
(security, contracts, failure modes) belong in blocking issues or missing edge
cases instead. Drop this section for docs that aren't designs._

## Missing edge cases

_States, inputs, or failures the doc does not cover._

## Terminology issues

_Inconsistent, unclear, or incorrect terms._

## Source/evidence gaps

_Places where the doc needs a verifiable source._

## Questions for the author

_What only the human author can resolve._
